name: Multiplexed DC (Kelvin-sense) characterization of thousands of 22 nm UTB-SOI transistors at 4.2 K on a liquid-helium dipping probe
plain_name: Screen thousands of chip transistors at once by dipping the chip in liquid helium
description: Test dies with on-die 1-to-1024 multiplexers are wire-bonded (50 bonds) to a daughter board that plugs into a multi-pin cryogenic socket on a dipping probe immersed in a liquid-helium bath (4.2 K); three SMUs with force/sense lines, DAC bias rails and kHz digital control over twisted-pair looms acquire Id-Vgs data for BSIM-IMG model cards.
keywords: Screen thousands of chip transistors at once by dipping the chip in liquid helium

sources.citation: Method for efficient large-scale cryogenic characterization of CMOS technologies (National Physical Laboratory / Quantum Motion / Univ. of Strathclyde, arXiv:2404.11451, 2024)

requirements.rationale: All devices are characterized isothermally at the liquid-helium temperature of 4.2 K.
The die is connected through a multi-pin socket for bias, digital and analog lines.
Optional: the reported wiring was two looms of 12 twisted pairs (48 conductors) for force/sense, bias and digital lines.
Optional: the source immersed the sample in a liquid-helium bath; a 4 K stage of another cryostat can substitute.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
